findings.quote: Neutralization is both double displacement and acid-base.
findings.problem: A general statement that fails at a known exception. The acids, bases and pH lesson, which this lesson sends the student to ('See the acids, bases and pH lesson'), defines neutralization as any acid-base reaction and gives $NH_3+HCl\rightarrow NH_4Cl$ as a neutralization (its Trap #4). That reaction has one product and no partner swap, so it is a combination, not a double displacement. The driving-force bullet 'Water forms. This happens when an acid meets a base.' fails on the same reaction, since no water forms. A student who learns both lessons gets two contradicting rules and misclassifies ammonia neutralizations.
findings.source: content/lessons/science/chemistry/acids-bases-ph.md, Neutralization section and Trap #4; OpenStax Chemistry 2e, 14.1 (Bronsted-Lowry acid-base reactions, NH3 + HCl); checklist B01; reader rules, Added after the Sol audit

findings.problem: The activity-series display has twelve symbols and eleven relation signs, each with relation spacing. It renders at roughly 30 em, wider than a phone screen at display size, so it will overflow or shrink. Earlier rounds split wide displays in Example #10 for this reason.
findings.source: Checklist L21; LSG Examples section (display equations narrow enough for a phone screen)

findings.quote: A weak electrolyte forms. This is a compound that stays mostly as molecules in water and gives few ions, such as a weak acid.
findings.problem: This driving-force bullet holds four sentences, and the bullet 'Water forms. This happens when an acid meets a base. It is called neutralization. See the acids, bases and pH lesson.' also holds four. The guide allows one to three short sentences per paragraph. The round-4 L22a paragraphs are fixed; these two bullets remain.
